- Role `default/app-config-reader` grants **only** `get configmaps app-config` (least-privilege grant).

**Diagnosis**

The in-cluster configuration reader is the `app` Deployment in namespace `default`. Its pod template runs an init container `read-config`, which must HTTP-GET `https://kubernetes.default.svc/api/v1/namespaces/default/configmaps/app-config` using the projected ServiceAccount token.

Evidence of the fault:
- Pod `app-65d788dd7b-dqvks`: `Init:Error`, 2/3 BackOff events, `Initialized=False`.
- `kubectl -n default logs ... --container=read-config` produced no output and then `BackOff restarting failed container read-config`.
- The same token-based curl command in the working ReplicaSet pods (e.g. `app-5c4859756d-5srgt`) succeeds, so image/network was fine — the call is denied by RBAC.

Root cause from cluster objects:
- Role `default/app-config-reader` grants **only** `get configmaps app-config` (least-privilege grant).
- RoleBinding `app-config-reader` bound it to subject `ServiceAccount/app-reader` in `default`.
- But the deployment sets `serviceAccountName: config-reader`, and ServiceAccount `app-reader` **does not exist**:
  `kubectl -n default get sa app-reader` → `Error from server (NotFound): serviceaccounts "app-reader" not found`.

The old ReplicaSet was already being replaced by the controller, so the broken SA name carried over into the new template; no other object in the namespace needed changing.

```
kubectl -n default patch rolebinding app-config-reader --type=merge \
  -p '{"subjects":[{"kind":"ServiceAccount","name":"config-reader","namespace":"default"}]}'
```

No rules were modified — still only `get` on one ConfigMap. No other SA, RoleBinding, or cluster resources touched; the ServiceAccount was pre-existing rather than created anew, and nothing else in the namespace exists (`serviceaccounts/config-reader`, `default`).
